import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

  | verum    => falsum

  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

informal_statement: The complexity of a formula and its negation are equal.
informal_proof:
To establish that the complexity of a formula \( \varphi \) and its negation \( \lnot \varphi \) are equal, we will use an inductive argument based on the structure of \( \varphi \). Complexity, in this context, refers to some measure of the formula's structural complexity, such as the depth of logical connectives or the number of atomic propositions it contains.

We proceed by induction on the structure of \( \varphi \):

1. **Atomic Formulas**: If \( \varphi \) is an atomic formula (e.g., \( P \)), both \( \varphi \) and \( \lnot \varphi \) have the same complexity since adding a negation does not introduce any new connectives or increase the structure beyond the atomic level.

2. **Negation of a Formula**: For a formula \( \varphi \) built using a logical connective, \( \lnot \varphi \) does not change the complexity because the negation operator is applied before \( \varphi \), but does not alter the structural components of \( \varphi \) itself.

3. **Conjunction and Disjunction**: For formulas \( \varphi_1 \) and \( \varphi_2 \), the complexity of \( \varphi_1 \land \varphi_2 \) and \( \varphi_1 \lor \varphi_2 \) remains the same. Applying negation does not affect the individual complexities of \( \varphi_1 \) and \( \varphi_2 \), so the complexity of their conjunction or disjunction remains unchanged.

4. **Implication**: For \( \varphi_1 \rightarrow \varphi_2 \), the complexity is determined by the complexities of \( \varphi_1 \) and \( \varphi_2 \). Negation applied to the entire implication \( \lnot (\varphi_1 \rightarrow \varphi_2) \) maintains the structural complexity since it only changes the truth value without altering the formula's architecture.

5. **Existential and Universal Quantifiers**: Finally, for formulas with quantifiers, such as \( \exists x \varphi(x) \) or \( \forall x \varphi(x) \), adding a negation results in a formula of the form \( \lnot \exists x \varphi(x) \) or \( \lnot \forall x \varphi(x) \), which respectively become \( \forall x \lnot \varphi(x) \) and \( \exists x \lnot \varphi(x) \). The complexity remains consistent since only the quantifier and the negation are altered without increasing the depth of the formula's structure.

Through each inductive step, we have accounted for how negation affects the formula's complexity across various logical constructs, ensuring that the complexity of \( \lnot \varphi \) aligns with that of \( \varphi \). The application of simplification lemmas ensures that our induction holds by maintaining these invariants at each step of the formula's construction.

Therefore, by induction, the complexity of \( \varphi \) is equal to the complexity of \( \lnot \varphi \) for all formulas \( \varphi \).

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  | verum    => falsum

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

variable {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language} {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*} {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}
informal_statement: For any language \( L \) and context \( \xi \), and for any \( n \), any semiformula \( \phi \) over \( L \) with context \( \xi \) at index \( n \) is provable.
informal_proof:
To establish that any semiformula \( \phi \) over a language \( L \) with context \( \xi \) at index \( n \) is provable, we proceed by systematically analyzing the cases defined by the recursive inductive type `rec'`:

1. **Base Cases**:
   - **Verum (⊤)**: By definition, the verum formula is always provable.
   - **Falsum (⊥)**: By definition, the falsum formula is always provable.

2. **Logical Connectives**:
   - **Conjunction (φ ∧ ψ)**: To prove \( φ \land ψ \), we first prove \( φ \) and then \( ψ \).
   - **Disjunction (φ ∨ ψ)**: To prove \( φ \lor ψ \), we consider which of \( φ \) or \( ψ \) is provable and prove the first one.
   - **Universal Quantification (∀xφ)**: To prove \( \forall xφ \), we assume \( x \) is fresh and prove \( φ \) under this assumption.
   - **Existential Quantification (∃xφ)**: To prove \( \exists xφ \), we can fix any \( x \) and prove \( φ \).

3. **Inductive Step**:
   - By applying the appropriate constructor in `rec'`, we handle each form of the semiformula \( \phi \):
     - For \( ⊤ \), use `hverum`.
     - For \( ⊥ \), use `hfalsum`.
     - For a relation \( rel(r, v) \), use `hrel`.
     - For a negation \( nrel(r, v) \), use `hnrel`.
     - For a conjunction \( \phi \land \psi \), use `hand`.
     - For a disjunction \( \phi \lor \psi \), use `hor`.
     - For a universal quantification \( \forall x\phi \), use `hall`.
     - For an existential quantification \( \exists x\phi \), use `hex`.

Each step ensures that the semiformula \( \phi \) is provable by breaking it down into its constituent parts and proving each part individually. This method covers all possible forms of semiformulas and thus ensures that any \( \phi \) is indeed provable.

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"

  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"

  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

content_full:
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

lemma neg_eq (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma ball_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∀[φ] ψ) = ∀' (φ ➝ ψ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [imp_eq]

def complexity {n : ℕ} : Semiformula L ξ n → ℕ
| ⊤        => 0
| ⊥        => 0
| rel _ _  => 0
| nrel _ _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

  constructor

  · exact congr_arg _

  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=

  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [imp_eq]

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: For any semiformula $\phi$, the complexity of an appropriately existentially quantified version of $\phi$ is equal to the complexity of $\phi$ plus one.
informal_proof: Consider a semiformula $\phi$. When we existentially quantify $\phi$, i.e., write $\exists'\phi$, we add one additional logical component: the existential quantifier. Assuming the complexity of a formula is measured by the number of such logical components it contains, the addition of one quantifier directly increases the complexity by one. import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

namespace LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula

variable {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language} {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*} {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}
informal_statement: For any semiformula $\phi$ in the language $L$ with $n+1$ variables, the complexity of the universally quantified formula $\forall \phi$ is equal to the complexity of $\phi$ plus one.
informal_proof: The universal quantification $\forall \phi$ introduces an additional layer of structure compared to $\phi$, specifically adding a universal quantifier which typically contributes to an increase in complexity by one. Since complexity measures the structural complexity of the formula, and adding a universal quantifier increases it by one, we have $\forall \phi$ has a complexity of $\phi$ plus one. This property is inherent to the way complexity is defined for semiformulas in the language $L$.

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

lemma neg_eq (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma ball_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∀[φ] ψ) = ∀' (φ ➝ ψ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg
C0_dependencies.content:
def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum

  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)

informal_statement: For any two logical formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the complexity of their disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ is equal to the maximum complexity of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ plus one.
informal_proof:
To determine the complexity of the disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$, we consider the complexities of the individual formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$. Suppose the complexity of $\varphi$ is $C(\varphi)$ and the complexity of $\psi$ is $C(\psi)$. 

When constructing the disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$, we add one additional layer of logical operation (the OR operation) on top of the formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$. This additional layer increases the complexity by one. Therefore, the complexity of $\varphi \lor \psi$ is determined by taking the maximum complexity between $C(\varphi)$ and $C(\psi)$ and then adding one to account for the OR operation.

Thus, the complexity of $\varphi \lor \psi$ is:
$$
C(\varphi \lor \psi) = \max\{C(\varphi), C(\psi)\} + 1
$$

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

lemma neg_eq (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma ball_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∀[φ] ψ) = ∀' (φ ➝ ψ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=
  by simp[ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

lemma neg_eq (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma ball_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∀[φ] ψ) = ∀' (φ ➝ ψ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: The complexity of the conjunction of two logical formulas is equal to the maximum complexity of each formula plus one.
informal_proof:
To determine the complexity of the conjunction ("φ and ψ") of two formulas φ and ψ, we consider their individual complexities. If φ has a complexity of m and ψ has a complexity of n, the complexity of "φ and ψ" is defined as the maximum of m and n plus one. This is because the conjunction introduces an additional layer of logical structure, increasing the complexity by one. 

For instance, if φ has a complexity of 2 and ψ has a complexity of 3, the conjunction φ and ψ would have a complexity of 4 (which is max(2,3) + 1). This definition ensures that the complexity reflects the deepest nesting level of logical operations in the formula, accurately capturing the structural complexity introduced by the conjunction.

Thus, by the definition of complexity in logical formulas, the conjunction of two formulas has a complexity equal to the maximum complexity of each formula plus one, which can be succinctly expressed as:

complexity("φ and ψ") = max(complexity(φ), complexity(ψ)) + 1

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

by simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=

  by simp[UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ :=

informal_statement: The complexity of the logical conjunction (AND) of two formulas is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities plus one.
informal_proof:
By definition, the complexity of a conjunction \( \varphi \land \psi \) is determined by considering the maximum complexity of its components \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \). Adding the conjunction operation increases the complexity by one step. Therefore, 

\[
\text{complexity}(\varphi \land \psi) = \max(\text{complexity}(\varphi), \text{complexity}(\psi)) + 1
\]
