import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg
C0_dependencies.content:
def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma neg_bex (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃[φ] ψ) = ∀[φ] ∼ψ := by
  simp [ball, bex, imp_eq]

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp [Wedge.wedge]

by simp[Vee.vee]

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

  | verum    => falsum

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ball (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀[φ] ψ) = ∃[φ] ∼ψ := by

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

For more complex formulas:
- Binary operations like conjunction (`φ ⋏ ψ`) and disjunction (`φ ⋎ ψ`) are assigned a complexity that is one greater than the maximum complexity of their operands. This accounts for the structure introduced by these operations.
- Quantified formulas like universal (`∀' φ`) and existential (`∃' φ`) quantifiers are assigned a complexity one greater than the complexity of their bound formula. This reflects the added structure from quantification.

The definition ensures that the complexity of a formula reflects the number of logical operations or quantifiers required to build it up from simpler components, thus providing a clear and systematic measure of complexity.

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := rfl

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v

  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

lemma neg_eq (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

lemma ball_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∀[φ] ψ) = ∀' (φ ➝ ψ) := rfl

lemma bex_eq (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : (∃[φ] ψ) = ∃' (φ ⋏ ψ) := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v

  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ

  vee := or

  bot := falsum

  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl

  and := fun _ _ => rfl

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  | verum    => falsum

  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

informal_statement: For any semiformula \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) in the language \( L \), the universal iteration of \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) over \( k \) terms being equal implies that \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) themselves are equal.
informal_proof:
We will prove this statement by induction on \( k \).

**Base Case (\( k = 0 \))**:
When \( k = 0 \), there are no terms to iterate over. Thus, the universal iteration of \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) over 0 terms is trivially equal to both \( \phi \) and \( \psi \). Therefore, \( \forall^{[0]} \phi = \phi \) and \( \forall^{[0]} \psi = \psi \). Hence, if \( \forall^{[0]} \phi = \forall^{[0]} \psi \), it immediately follows that \( \phi = \psi \).

**Inductive Step**:
Assume that for some \( k \geq 0 \), the statement holds: if \( \forall^{[k]} \phi = \forall^{[k]} \psi \), then \( \phi = \psi \). We need to show that the statement holds for \( k + 1 \).

Consider \( \forall^{[k+1]} \phi \) and \( \forall^{[k+1]} \psi \). By definition, this involves iterating the universal quantification one more time. Suppose \( \forall^{[k+1]} \phi = \forall^{[k+1]} \psi \). Then, by unwinding the definition, this implies that \( \forall^{[k]} ( \forall \cdot \phi ) = \forall^{[k]} ( \forall \cdot \psi ) \). Applying the inductive hypothesis, we conclude that \( \forall \cdot \phi = \forall \cdot \psi \). Finally, by the base case or the structure of the formulas, we infer that \( \phi = \psi \).

Thus, by the principle of mathematical induction, the statement holds for all \( k \).

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v

  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ

  vee := or

  bot := falsum

  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl

  and := fun _ _ => rfl

  ex := ex

  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

@[simp] lemma neg_univClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∀* φ) = ∃* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]

@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]
annotation:
@[simp] lemma neg_exClosure (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(∃* φ) = ∀* ∼φ := by
  /-
    L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
    ξ : Type u_1
    n : Nat
    φ : LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula L ξ n
    ⊢ Eq (LO.Tilde.tilde (LO.exClosure φ)) (LO.univClosure (LO.Tilde.tilde φ))
  -/
                  /-
                    🎉 no goals
                  -/
  induction n <;> simp [univClosure, exClosure, *]
                  /-
                    🎉 no goals
                  -/

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

namespace LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula

variable {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language} {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*} {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}
informal_statement: For any two well-formed formulas φ and ψ in a language L, if their universal closures are identical, then the formulas themselves are identical. This establishes that universal closure uniquely determines a formula.
informal_proof:
We will prove this statement by induction on the complexity (where complexity is measured by the number of quantifier blocks) of the formulas φ and ψ.

**Base Case (n = 0):**
When n = 0, φ and ψ are atomic formulas (since they have no quantifiers). Assume that their universal closures are the same. Since no quantification is involved, φ must be identical to ψ. Thus, the base case holds.

**Inductive Step:**
Assume that the statement holds for all formulas of complexity n. Let φ and ψ be formulas of complexity n + 1. Without loss of generality, suppose φ starts with a universal quantifier (∀). Then, φ has the form ∀x₁,…,xₖ(φ'), where φ' is a formula of complexity n. Similarly, ψ would have a similar structure.

If �������� offence of φ equals �������� offence of ψ, then the universal closures at complexity n for φ' and ψ' must be equal (by the inductive definition of universal closure). # Formulas of first-order logic

The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.neg
C0_dependencies.content:
def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

  | falsum   => verum

  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

informal_statement: For any two formulas φ and ψ in a given formal language, if φ is equivalent to ψ, then universally quantifying both with "for all" preserves this equivalence. Conversely, if the universal quantifications of φ and ψ are equivalent, then φ and ψ themselves must be equivalent.
informal_proof:
To establish this, we consider two formulas φ and ψ that are equivalent, denoted φ = ψ. When we universally quantify both sides with "for all," we obtain ∀φ and ∀ψ. Since φ and ψ are equivalent, it follows that ∀φ and ∀ψ are also equivalent. This preservation of equivalence under universal quantification is fundamental in formal logic.

Conversely, if the universal quantifications ∀φ and ∀ψ are equivalent, then φ must be equivalent to ψ. This is because the universal quantifier does not introduce any new information beyond the original formulas; it simply applies a condition across all members of a domain. Therefore, the equivalence of the quantified formulas implies the equivalence of the original statements.

Thus, the equivalence of φ and ψ is preserved under universal quantification in both directions.

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∃' φ) = ∀' ∼φ := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Term
import Foundation.Logic.Predicate.Quantifier

/-!
# Formulas of first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformula L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

inductive Semiformula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformula L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | nrel   {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformula L ξ n

abbrev Formula (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformula L ξ 0

abbrev Sentence (L : Language) := Formula L Empty

abbrev Semisentence (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformula (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformula L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormula (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformula L 0

namespace Semiformula

variable
  {L : Language} {L₁ : Language} {L₂ : Language} {L₃ : Language}
  {ξ ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Type*}
  {n n₁ n₂ n₂ m m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ}

def neg {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → Semiformula L ξ n
  | verum    => falsum
  | falsum   => verum
  | rel r v  => nrel r v
  | nrel r v => rel r v
  | and φ ψ  => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ   => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | all φ    => ex (neg φ)
  | ex φ     => all (neg φ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

instance : DeMorgan (Semiformula L ξ n) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  imply := fun _ _ => rfl
  and := fun _ _ => rfl
  or := fun _ _ => rfl
  neg := neg_neg

instance : Quantifier (Semiformula L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr {n} : Semiformula L ξ n → String
  | ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | nrel (arity := 0) r _     => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | nrel (arity := _ + 1) r v => "\\lnot {" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformula L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Semiformula L ξ n) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(rel r v) = nrel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_nrel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : ∼(nrel r v) = rel r v := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_all (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : ∼(∀' φ) = ∃' ∼φ := rfl
